subject: Next steps — Deployment residency & connectivity clarifications for Astraeon Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@astraeonhealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@astraeonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment residency & connectivity clarifications (summary + asks)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Below is a compact summary of what we heard and the specific clarifying questions / asks so we can scope a Private/VPC or on‑prem deployment that meets Astraeon’s compliance needs. Please flag anything we missed.

Key goals you stated
- Keep PHI data processing entirely within Astraeon-managed networks and cloud accounts.
- No outbound egress to third-party endpoints for model payloads (strict allowlist).
- Bring-your-own-KMS (customer-managed keys; HSM/KMS required).
- Retention and audit trail: preserve request/response traces and access logs for at least 7 years for regulatory audits.

Primary constraints mentioned
- Production will be in a dedicated VPC in AWS GovCloud (us‑gov-west) — no cross‑region replication unless explicitly approved.
- Minimal internet-facing endpoints; all control-plane comms to Redwood must traverse an approved transit path or be brokered through a private peering/Direct Connect.
- Temporary on‑prem air‑gapped evaluation for pilot (3–4 weeks) before full rollout.

Clarifying questions / asks (please respond inline where helpful)
1) Network topology: Do you prefer PrivateLink endpoints vs. transit VPC + route tables for Redwood control-plane? If PrivateLink, we’ll enumerate required NLB target groups and ENI counts.
2) KMS: Confirm whether keys will be stored in a customer HSM in the same VPC or in a centralized account (we may need key policy examples).
3) Audit logs: Which supplier of log collection do you want us to integrate with (Splunk/Datadog/CloudWatch Logs)? Also confirm retention policy (7 years is noted — do you need immutable storage?)
4) Pilot airgap: proposed dates for the on‑prem pilot window and whether a temporary network jumpbox is acceptable for initial telemetry.

Attached I’ve included a one‑page Ops asks doc and an anonymized CSV of the network sticky points we discussed.

Proposed next actions (owner / ETA)
- Redwood to provide a short MOP (method of procedure) for PrivateLink and Direct Connect options — Ben (48 business hours)
- Astraeon to confirm KMS topology and log vendor — Sarah (by 2029-05-22)
- Schedule a technical deep‑dive with Infra + Security (30–60m) — Marissa to propose slots for 2029-05-24/25

If that looks right I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical deep‑dive and a stub SOW to kick procurement.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Enterprise GTM | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑0134

Attachments: redwood-deployment-asks-20290520.pdf (pdf stub), astraeon-network-notes-raw.csv (csv stub)
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@astraeonhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@astraeonhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 17:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment residency & connectivity clarifications (summary + asks)

Marissa — thanks for the concise summary, that aligns well with our expectations. A few clarifications: 

- PrivateLink is our preferred pattern for control-plane connectivity to avoid exposing route tables through a transit VPC — we can provision endpoints in the app account. Please send the required service names and anticipated ENI counts so we can size subnets.
- KMS: we will use a centralized HSM in our security account (we manage keys via AWS CloudHSM + KMS). Key policies will be provided by our security team but expect customer‑managed keys with strict usage policies.
- Logs: we use a Splunk heavy‑forwarder for long‑term retention. Yes — immutable archival (S3 Glacier Deep Archive) for 7 years is a hard requirement.
- Pilot: We can do the on‑prem airgapped evaluation starting the week of 2029‑06‑10 for approximately 3 weeks. A temporary jumpbox that only allows outbound on an approved port is acceptable for secure telemetry during pilot.

One additional ask: procurement will need a short data flow diagram that highlights where tokenization/anonymization happens (if any) and all points where PHI could be in flight. If you can include that in the SOW draft it will speed signoff.

Tom and I are available for the deep‑dive on 2029‑05‑24 at 10:00am PT if that works.

—Sarah
Director, Cloud Engineering | Astraeon Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@astraeonhealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@astraeonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment residency & connectivity clarifications (summary + asks)

Thanks Sarah — this is excellent and very clear. Quick responses inline: 

- PrivateLink preferred: noted. Ben, I’ll ask you to draft the PrivateLink service names and a short ENI/subnet sizing table.
- KMS centralized HSM: noted — we’ll include key policy examples in the security appendix of the SOW.
- Splunk + immutable archive: understood. We’ll call out the Splunk heavy‑forwarder integration and S3 Glacier archival workflow in the ops section.
- Pilot window 2029‑06‑10: good — we’ll target that for the on‑prem evaluation.

Action list + owners: 
- Ben Carter: PrivateLink service names + ENI sizing (deliverable: PrivateLink MOP) — due 2029‑05‑22
- Marissa: SOW stub with data flow diagram + security appendix (deliverable: SOW v0.1) — due 2029‑05‑23
- Stephanie Nguyen: Prelim support pricing for a 3‑week airgapped pilot + reserved capacity options — due 2029‑05‑23
- Astraeon (Sarah): KMS policy sample + confirmation of Splunk forwarder hostnames — due 2029‑05‑22

I’ll put the 30‑minute deep‑dive on the calendar for 2029‑05‑24 10:00am PT and include a short agenda: 1) network topology choices (PrivateLink vs. transit), 2) KMS/HSM integration patterns, 3) pilot MOP checklist.

If anything slips/changes, call me directly.

Marissa

---
Attachment: redwood-deployment-asks-20290520.pdf (pdf stub)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: deployment residency & connectivity clarifications (internal)

Quick internal note before the deep‑dive:

- I’ll prepare PrivateLink service names and an ENI sizing table — initial estimate: 2 NLBs per region, up to 6 ENIs depending on AZ distribution. Will validate against GovCloud quotas.
- For the pilot, we should propose a telemetry-only jumpbox that strips PHI at the edge (tokenization) before any outbound traces — that addresses their immutable archive ask while keeping audit evidence.
- Stephanie — can you draft a pilot pricing line that isolates the 3‑week airgapped effort (engineering + on‑site support) and a follow‑on monthly reserved capacity price? I’ll include the expected infra delta for HSM connections.

Ben
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
